answer: The canyon multiplier is published, charged in anchor, and inlet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 18 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4580 identities would post 757 proofs and burn roughly 36 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
